Here now, as had happened with the German **gold-makers** <note>original: "Goldmachern"; a term often used somewhat mockingly for those obsessed with the literal transmutation of lead into gold rather than spiritual enlightenment.</note>, a new lamenting, complaining, and excusing began. In the absence of Mercury, so many coals, **retorts**, and **crucibles** <note>standard glass and ceramic tools used for distillation and melting in an alchemist's workshop.</note> had shattered, and during their previous laboring, so many fatalities and mishaps had occurred again, that these laborants did not know how to sufficiently describe their chemical accidents and misery. 

When the aforementioned laborants had brought forth their complaints in great length and quantity, Mercury interrupted them with the following words: "All your complaints—which are partly not unknown to me—are not sufficient to exempt you from the commanded journey; see here, this is what makes such complaints and your objections invalid." With these words, he simultaneously handed over the small package full of **Chemical Gold**, which had been given to him, to the most prominent chemists—specifically to one among them who sat in a costly **chaise** <note>a light, open carriage.</note> drawn by two beautiful Spanish stallions—with the report and command that they should now, without delay, select ten **deputy chemists** from among themselves and the laborants and gold-makers found in Asia. He gave them the Chemical Gold entrusted to them in the name of the goddess Pallas (which consisted of the aforementioned types of coin) for their maintenance and travel expenses, and instructed how these men should behave among the gold-makers...

Mercury took to the air once again; while flying, he thought of the Island of the Sages <note>The "Island of the Sages" (Insula Sapientum) is a common allegorical location in alchemical literature, representing a hidden place where true adepts reside and where the secrets of nature are guarded.</note>, and at the same time of his promise—namely, to visit the inhabitants there as often as the opportunity might arise. He floated back and forth for a long while before he could find this island again, but as soon as he reached it, he descended with delight and was received and welcomed by its inhabitants with great joy. They led him into their caves and showed him many more secret things than before, because they could now be certain of his discretion. Although they did not wish to recognize or tolerate any **Superior** <note>original: "Superiorem"; a ruler or higher authority.</note> over themselves, they had nevertheless resolved in Mercury's absence to make their newly arrived friend and guest, Mercury, their king—albeit under certain conditions.

Therefore, they took their leave and asked that Mercury might take it in good part if they left him a little alone and withdrew; they said that all the inhabitants of this island would soon appear before him again and present a proposal that would, hopefully, not be unpleasant to him. Mercury, who could not guess their intention, waited in his magnificent, enclosed room—whose walls and doors were of the finest gold—with longing for the return of the departed inhabitants of the Island of the Sages, but even more for the proposal they had mentioned. 

However, the aforementioned inhabitants did not assemble very quickly, as they undertake all their affairs with the greatest caution. Once they were together, they reviewed those **Articles and Laws** <note>original: "Articul und Leges"; these represent the "laws" of chemical fixation that bind the volatile spirit.</note> which they intended to present and read to Mercury during their planned election. They reviewed them more than 3, 6, 8, even 9 times before they reached a final conclusion. Because of this, the time grew quite long for Mercury, so that in his naturally intense longing, he resolved to leave the room in which he found himself. He therefore approached the door, which he found secured with a golden lock and bolt. He could have opened and pushed both aside with little effort; however, as soon as he approached the golden lock, door, and bolt and laid his hand upon them, he remained standing as if fettered out of love for the gold. When he turned toward the walls and windows, he grew rigid and lost his otherwise swift movement. Thus, Mercury was forced against his will—with both the greatest patience and impatience—to await the arrival and return of the aforementioned inhabitants who had left him. 

After an hour had passed, all the inhabitants of the said island, young and old, gathered before the room in which they had left Mercury. They opened the door and asked Mercury for forgiveness for having left him so long...

## Address and Laws of the Inhabitants of the Island of the Sages to Mercury.

Invaluable Mercury, since we are sufficiently assured of your discretion and loyalty, and have abundantly perceived and felt your virtue and goodness spreading over us and our island; we, your assembled friends and co-administrators of this our island, are unanimously willing to make you a king—specifically, our **King**—yet without any lordship <note>original: "Herrſchafft"; here meaning sovereign power or dominion.</note> and without our subjection; both of which can conveniently happen and exist with the greatest dignity. For we elevate and raise you like the finest gold <note>The "elevation" or *exaltatio* refers to an alchemical process where a substance is purified and its potency is increased.</note>, and thereby we hand over to you such a government that you require no lordship over us; we cannot be subject to you, because in your elevation we rule over you, and after this, together with you, we make the world subject to us <note>This paradox describes the relationship between the alchemist and their material: the alchemist "rules" the substance by perfecting it, and once perfected, the substance (the Philosopher's Stone) allows the alchemist to master the natural world.</note>. We hope, therefore, all the more that you will accept our proposal and consent to our drafted following Laws <note>original: "Leges"</note> and Statutes, and hold them as acceptable.

## Laws or Statutes.

->1.<-

->Mercury shall be our King.<-

->2.<-

->But never rule over us.<-

->3.<-

->Just as we also bind ourselves to no subjection.<-

Mercury listened to all of this with the greatest composure, and for a long time, he did not know what he should decide. At first, he excused himself because, as is well known, he was the messenger of the gods and was not permitted to remain permanently in one place, as he was sent now here, now there—indeed, throughout the entire world.

Furthermore, he was by nature not suited to take anything permanent upon himself, because he consisted of nothing but a fleeting essence, which he also loved, as he was not called "Living Mercury" <note>original: "Mercurius Vivus"; the common Latin term for liquid quicksilver</note> for nothing.

The inhabitants of the oft-mentioned island <note>original: "Insul"</note> countered that, as far as the first point was concerned, this was not unknown to them, and they neither wanted to nor could hinder him in any way; but they also knew how the gods permitted him to divide himself into an innumerable multitude of small particles <note>original: "Particulgen"</note>, and that Aeolus <note>The god of the winds</note> had to lead and carry him around the whole world, and thus also over their island. They would be satisfied with whatever Aeolus would bring to them.

Regarding the second point, the goddess Pallas <note>Pallas Athena, the goddess of wisdom</note> herself had given them the instruction and the freedom to accommodate Mercury in such a way that he should feel no desire to leave them.

Upon the placement of the third and final crown, the people cried out:
> Long live Mercury in his essential and enduring dignity and royal splendor, without destruction, unto our Art.

## Chapter IX.

1. Mercury desires to give an oral report to the goddess Pallas <note>Pallas Athena, often representing Wisdom or the guiding intelligence in alchemical allegories.</note> concerning the commission <note>original: *Commission*; an official task or diplomatic mission.</note> entrusted to him.

5. The chemical <term>processes</term> <note>The specific sequences of operations (heating, distilling, etc.) used to transform base metals into gold.</note> and writings of the European and Asian gold-makers.

After Mercury had stayed for some time on the Island of the Wise, he nevertheless felt a desire to bring the commission he had accepted from Pallas on his other journey to a praiseworthy conclusion, and to provide a verbal and precise report of his recent activities. For this reason, he had his fellow governors, the inhabitants of the Island of the Wise, assemble and come before him, explained his departure and its cause to them, and assured them of his eventual return in the following manner.

# Greeting and Farewell Speech of Mercury to the Inhabitants of the Island of the Wise.

### Well-experienced, ruling Masters of Nature and co-governors of this Island.

I have remained with you for as long as you yourselves desired, so that I might be useful to you at my own cost <note>original: "mit meinem Schaden"; in alchemical allegory, this often refers to the "suffering" or transformation of the substance during the work</note>, though also for my own and your best interest. Although I otherwise flee what you seek and hate what you desire, I also yearn for what you demand of me: which is perfection and rest <note>Rest, or "Ruhe," refers to "fixation," the state where the volatile Mercury is made stable and no longer evaporates when heated.</note>. Both I have found with you, and you with me. Wise and understanding men, your science alone, your uncommon knowledge of Nature, has caused my stay among you; and it is this very thing that binds me to assure you herewith of my infallible return.

Know, however, that time and the hours call me to appear before the Goddess, who gave you the understanding, power, and ability to deal with me as you have done. So that Pallas, who is well-disposed toward both you and me, may not be offended by my lingering or your delay, grant that I may enjoy the freedom I requested from the very beginning: to depart from you, approach the throne of Pallas, and personally deliver a verbal report regarding the commission <note>original: "Commission"; the official task or diplomatic mission Mercury was sent to perform.</note> entrusted to me. Thus, we need not fear the wrath of said Goddess, but may rather hold the hope of being together again soon—all the more peacefully and with the same pleasure with which I now leave you.

As soon as Mercury had ended his speech, he returned to the green square where he had previously been crowned, and the people assembled in their usual numbers. After they had collectively consented to Mercury’s desire and departure, they cried out three times: "Long live Mercury, royal co-governor of our island! May Aeolus <note>The ruler of the winds in Greek mythology, responsible here for a favorable flight.</note> lead him with nothing but luck and wellness before the throne of Pallas, and so back to us again!"

Thereupon, Mercury soared into the heights with his wings in his customary manner, and thus left this island and its inhabitants.

After Mercury had once again traversed the air for a considerable time, striving to take the most direct path and flight toward the throne of Pallas, he happened to catch sight of the ten appointed Asian chemists <note>original: "Chymisten"; early modern chemists or alchemists.</note>,

And when he had been well received and welcomed by the entire assembly of goddesses and Apollo, and the quartering of the chemists was approved, Mercury—at the request of Pallas—recounted what had happened to him anew with the goldmakers in Europe and Asia, and particularly what had occurred regarding the *Chemical Gold* <term>Chemical Gold: Unlike "vulgar" or natural gold, this refers to gold produced or transformed through alchemical means, often symbolizing the successful completion of a stage of the Great Work.</term> he had brought with him (though he remained entirely silent regarding the Island of the Wise). 

When he reached the point in his story where all the goldmakers, both in Europe and in Asia, did not even recognize the *Chemical Gold* and hardly wanted to accept it as valid, all the goddesses and Apollo wondered not a little: that people who had read so many chemical books, people who wanted to make gold for so many years, people who had squandered all their possessions in their laboratories <note>original: "verlaboriret"; a specific term for losing one's fortune through failed alchemical experiments.</note>, did not even know *Chemical Gold*. Yet they had always worked away blindly, in their simplicity, without any true knowledge of Nature, and thus without pause or ceasing, violently wasting their fortunes year after year. The gods therefore became all the more eager to hear what truly characterized this strange kind of people...

# Chemical Writings and Processes of the Laborants from Europe.
## The 1st Process.
### The Great Secret and Mystery <note>original: "Secretum & Arcanum Magnum"</note>, how one should make and prepare the Mercury of the Philosophers <note>original: "Mercurium Philosophorum"; a purified, "living" form of mercury believed by alchemists to be the essential starting material for the Philosopher's Stone.</note> and the Oil of Salt <note>original: "Oleum Salis"; in 16th-century alchemy, this often referred to a concentrated acid or a specialized salt derivative used as a solvent.</note>, and finally the true and genuine Tincture <note>A "tincture" is a potent alchemical substance capable of transforming or "dyeing" base metals into gold or silver.</note> for all metals, to tincture them into truly good, permanent gold; written to a distinguished Doctor by Bartel Veltenbergen; September 22, 1553.

My favorable, dear Mr. Doctor, very worthy and trusted friend! Hereby I reveal and send to you the entire art of all metals, and the true, genuine tincture of all metals; I write this with my own hand, which you know quite well, with all circumstances and procedures, for I have omitted no point. Rather, I send and transmit it to you just as I have worked it myself and earned over 16,000 gold guilders <note>A "gold guilder" (Gold-Gulden) was a high-value gold coin used throughout the Holy Roman Empire; 16,000 would have been an immense fortune.</note> with it in three years; and certainly, I would have acquired twice as much again if I had wished, but I am well satisfied that I have raised myself out of the dust of poverty and obtained such great wealth for myself through it in so short a time. Now, however, it is my only and heartfelt plea to you: that you would keep this great secret hidden, as truly as your worldly and eternal welfare is dear to you, work in silence, hide it from the world, and do not let this so precious treasure fall into the hands of the ignorant, for I am not minded to [reveal] such a secret...

## The Second Process.

# To bring one Loth of Gold into and out of a Mark of Silver.
<note>A "Loth" was a small unit of weight, about 1/16th of a Mark (~15 grams). This title suggests a process of "transmuting" a portion of a silver mass into gold.</note>

Take Spirit of Nitre <term>Spirit of Nitre: Nitric acid.</term> which is well dephlegmated <note>original: "dephlegmiret"; meaning the "phlegm" or water has been removed to concentrate the acid.</note>, as much as is sufficient <note>original: "q. s." or *quantum satis*.</note>; pour it over as much as you like <note>original: "q. l." or *quantum libet*.</note> of well-purified Mercury, so that it dissolves therein; then draw off the solution 4 to 6 times by cohobating <term>cohobation: The process of repeatedly redistilling a liquid over the solid residue from which it was just distilled to increase its "potency."</term>. Afterward, pour fresh Spirit of Nitre over it again and draw this off also 3 times. Repeat this work of drawing off and pouring on fresh Spirit of Nitre another 4 to 5 times, so the Mercury remains lying at the bottom. Furthermore, take Alum and Vitriol, two parts of each <note>original: "aa. p. ij." or *ana partes duas*.</note>, and 1 part Nitre; distill these, well-mixed, through a retort quite carefully. In this distillate, dissolve half a pound <note>original: "℔ß"; the symbol for half a pound.</note>. Then take 24 Loth of this and dissolve 8 Loth of copper <note>original: "Kupffer"</note> in it, and add 4 Loth of distilled wine vinegar to it;

In like manner, dissolve 8 Loth of iron filings <term>Limatura Martis: Iron filings; Mars is the alchemical name for iron.</term> just as you did the copper. When the metals are dissolved, draw off the solvent <term>menstruum: A solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solids.</term> from each separately 3 times, and on the last time, until it is completely dry <note>original: "ad siccitatem usque".</note>. Afterward, dissolve these metallic calxes <term>calx: The powdery residue left after a metal has been roasted or dissolved in acid; an oxide.</term> in Spirit of Urine <term>Spirit of Urine: A solution of ammonia.</term>, and the solution from the Mars [iron] will become red, but from the Venus [copper] it will become blue. Then digest each "saffron" <term>Crocus: A fine powder produced from a metal, named for its color (like the saffron flower).</term> in a vial for 3 to 4 weeks, and if any Spirit of Urine remains, draw it off gently from both powders.

NB. The test for this is: that they no longer smoke when they are sprinkled onto a hot metal plate.

When you have prepared them thus, mix both together—namely the powder of Venus and the powder of Mars—and add an equal weight of Sal Ammoniac <note>original: "Solarmoniac"; ammonium chloride.</note>; sublimate <term>sublimation: Heating a substance so it turns into vapor and then solidifies again as a purified crust.</term> them 3 to 4 times together, and indeed first with a gentle fire, but afterward with a quite strong fire, so that the matter rises. This sublimate becomes as beautiful a red as the loveliest rose;

Now take this obtained red sublimate <term>Sublimate: A solid substance produced by heating a material until it turns to vapor and then collecting the cooled deposit.</term>, boil it in an iron pan with water over a flame so that the sal ammoniac <note>original: "Salmiac"; ammonium chloride, used as a flux and cleaning agent.</note> dissolves; thus the sulfur will separate from the iron <note>original: "Marte"</note> and copper <note>original: "Venere"</note> and fall to the bottom.

## The 3rd Process.
### To multiply gold through silver and mercury.

Take 4 Loth of pure gold, 2 Loth of pure good silver, and 1 Loth of well-purified mercury. Amalgamate these 3 pieces in the best way according to the known method. Put this amalgam into a glass retort or phial, and place it well-secured over the fire for 30 to 40 days; thus the amalgam will turn into a blood-red powder. To this powder, add well-purified mercury again and digest <note>A process of gentle, consistent heating.</note> again until the mercury becomes fixed and fire-resistant.

Repeat this addition and fixation of mercury 4 times, and then dissolve the resulting red powder with the red solvent <term>Menstruum: A solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solids.</term> <note>original: "Menstruo rubro"</note> described below, which consists of salt, saltpeter, live sulfur, and Roman vitriol <note>Iron sulfate.</note>, as well as one pound each of iron filings <note>original: "Limatura Martis"</note>. After distillation, this solvent also appears red.

Distill the solution and draw off this solvent from the dissolved matter again according to the art several times, or repeat this dissolving and drawing off until the solvent comes over white.

The matter remaining in the retort should then be further dissolved in distilled mercurial vinegar <note>original: "aceto mercuriali"</note>, filtered, clarified, and drawn off again as is customary. Afterward, dissolve the matter once more in distilled rain <note>The text ends mid-word: "Regens[wasser]" (rainwater), commonly used in alchemy as a pure source of water.</note>

## The 4th Process.

### This presents a universal work.

Take: 1/2 pound <note>original symbol: "℔. ß."</note> of the best steel <note>original: "Chalybis optimi"</note>, 1 pound <note>original symbol: "℔. j."</note> of Hungarian antimony <note>original: "Antimonii Ungarici"</note> (but of the ore <note>original: "Minera"</note>, 4 Loth <note>Approximately 2 ounces or 60 grams.</note> more); hammer the steel thin and harden it in water, then break it into small pieces. Put these into a good and large melting crucible <term>Crucible: A ceramic or metal container used for melting materials at very high temperatures.</term>, and cover it well so that no coals fall inside. Afterwards, let it heat thoroughly in a wind furnace <term>Wind Furnace: A furnace designed to reach high temperatures through a strong draft of air.</term> until the steel glows welding-white. Then add the powdered antimony spoon by spoon, and when it flows properly, add pure, dry, well-crushed saltpeter <term>Saltpeter: Potassium nitrate, used here as a flux to help the metals melt and to burn off impurities.</term> successively. Cover the crucible tightly and bank it all around with coals; then let it melt at a very high heat and a good melting fire. ## The Oil of Salt, or what is called the Leonine Blood.

Take the purest Hungarian gold <note>original: *Auri Ungarici puriſſimi*</note>, as much as you like <note>original: *q. l.* or *quantum libet*</note>. Then pour fresh *Aqua Chusan* upon it again and let it putrefy for 14 days, well-sealed. Afterward, draw the water off from it again until it reaches an oily consistency, and putrefy it once more for 14 days with fresh *Aqua Chusan* as before. Then test whether the gold has surrendered itself to spirituality <note>In alchemy, "spirituality" refers to a substance becoming volatile, capable of rising or being distilled.</note>. If it flows upon a glowing coal, then it is spiritual; if not, then putrefy it again with fresh *Chusan*-water. When it has finally become spiritual enough, then coagulate and fix it in a glass into a stone until nothing smokes anymore; thus you have the **Red Lion** <term>Red Lion: A symbolic name for a high-stage alchemical substance, often the solar or gold-based catalyst in the "Great Work."</term>. You should make this spiritual again with the *Chusan*-water and putrefy it for 14 days; then distill it in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*</note> to an oily state; thus there remains a blood-red liquor, and this is the **Leonine Blood**.

We certainly have many and varied processes in Germany now, some of which are very costly, as they require not only an initial investment of 6, 8, to 20,000 florins <term>fl.: Florins, a common currency in the Holy Roman Empire.</term>, but also a very strong fire for 2, 3, 4, or more years, and thus a quite expensive amount of coal and, in part, wood. And it is these very processes that have occupied us **laborants** <note>laboratory workers or practical alchemists</note> in Germany until now; and because we have always worked at them fruitlessly, we have for the most part been ruined. Nevertheless, we still work at them hopefully. However, we have resolved that if we achieve nothing further with the aforementioned long and costly processes, we shall adopt the previously described short and less expensive processes, which we have partly selected from various authors following philosophical-chemical counsel, and partly received from true friends as manuscripts. These we wish to lay at the feet of the goddess Pallas <note>Pallas Athena, the goddess of wisdom, signifying that these methods are dedicated to true knowledge.</note> before they become the fashion among us and are begun like the previous ones.

## The 2nd Process.
### A Tincture of which 1 part, applied to 100 parts of other metals in flux, shall transform them into good, stable silver.

If you wish to augment <note>to increase the potency or volume</note> this tincture, then soak the Stone or the mass with three times as much of the mentioned water and proceed with it as before; then your Stone is perfected.

## The 3rd Process.

### This has been extracted from a hidden manuscript, represents a Universal Work, and was found among the treasury of certain Egyptian books.

It does nothing further except dissolve a perfect body into a spiritual-volatile essence, as follows here.

Sublimate the risen Mercury once more; take it and sublimate it yet again with as much fresh calcined alum as before. And for the third time, take 12 Loth of Coaldin and 8 Loth of calcined Giniton, mixing the Mercury into it and grinding it with half as much calcined alum, then sublimate it. This sublimate should be sublimated one final time, but only in calcined alum.

This work must be performed with fresh Coaldin and calcined Giniton 6 times; then the Mercury is prepared and will be found for the last time in the sublimation vessel. Grind this small, put it into a urinal-glass <note>a pear-shaped glass flask with a long neck, named for its resemblance to a medical vessel</note>, with the top well-sealed with luting <note>an airtight clay or paste seal</note>, and set it in horse-manure <note>original: *Roß-Mist*; used as a source of gentle, constant fermentation heat</note> for 14 days and nights, so that your Mercury turns to water. Distill this in a water bath <note>original: *B. M.*, for *Balneum Mariae*</note> so that the water rises over; pour it back into the glass and distill it again. Do this "up and down" distillation 4 times, or even more, until this Mercury enters into the four elements and is no longer Mercury, but is, by itself, a pure, bright, and fiery water, invisible <note>original: *invisibile*</note>. And this water must be kept as securely as possible, otherwise it will vanish immediately, for it has been destroyed into the four elements.

### ->Now the gold is purged, resolved with the completed key into a spiritual essence, and also separated and coagulated.<-

Take the purged gold, put it into a urinal-glass with a long neck, and pour the mercurial water over it so that it is well covered. Seal the glass with luting, and set it in gentle heat in a water bath for 3 days and nights, so that only the vapor rises. In this way, the gold becomes spiritual <note>volatile or refined into a non-metallic state</note> and fleeting because of the water. Pour the water off gradually and gently. Take the spiritual gold in the well-sealed glass and set it in ashes, placed as deep as the matter can be seen. The ashes should lie in a very thin earthen vessel, and under the vessel, place a lamp burning oil with 6 thick twine threads <note>original: *Zwirns-Faden*; the number of threads in the wick precisely controlled the temperature before the invention of thermometers</note>. This shall stand for 30 days and nights in such heat. Afterward, one should make a wick of 8 thick twine threads and maintain it in steady heat for just as long—namely, 30 days. After that, use 10 thick twine threads for 30 days, then 20 thick threads for 15 days and nights; thus the spiritual gold becomes once more...

## Now occurs the Division, and thereafter the Viscosification.

Take the gold that has been made fixed and divide it into two equal parts. Keep one part; the other part should be ground small. Put it into a glass and pour the aforementioned Mercurial Water over it so that it is slightly covered. Place it in a <term>B. M.</term> <note>original: *Balneum Mariae*; a warm water bath used for gentle, even heating</note> for three days and nights. Thus, this part will all become spiritual and volatile again; that is to say, it is **viscosified** and led into the **First Matter** <note>original: *primam materiam*; the primordial, formless state of matter sought by alchemists as the starting point for transmutation</note>. This is the second Solution, and after the first fixing, it is the true First Matter. Within this lies the great **Secret** <note>original: *Arcanum*</note> of the **Tincture**. Anyone who calls the first dissolution the First Matter is wrong, for that is merely a dissolved spiritual body which has been made fixed and properly shaped again through fire.

## Now follows the final work, and it is precipitated into a Stone.

Take then the First Matter, which you have viscosified with the Mercurial Water. Gently pour the Mercurial Water off it, dry it, and then grind it together with the other part that you kept earlier. Put them together into a <term>urinal-glass</term> <note>a pear-shaped glass flask with a long neck</note>. Let it be well-sealed <note>original: *versigilliret*; likely referring to the "Seal of Hermes," an airtight glass seal</note> and fixed in ashes, using a lamp-wick made of seven-fold thick twine in an oil lamp for twenty-one days and nights; thus the work will turn **black** <note>the *Nigredo* stage, representing putrefaction or death</note>. Thereafter, make the wick ten threads thick and let it stand for fifteen days and nights; it will turn **green and yellow** in color. Then, for ten days with a twelve-thread wick, it will become **white** <note>the *Albedo* stage, representing purification</note>, and the work is perfectly fixed, fire-proof, and righteous. Then, simply let the work stand with a great fire until it becomes **red as scarlet** <note>the *Rubedo* stage, the final perfection</note>; then the Tincture is ready and precipitated, fluid and penetrating. Thus is the right, true **Universal** <note>the Universal Medicine or Philosopher's Stone</note> now ready and perfect, with which to tincture many thousands of parts when it is resolved again. There follows how one should tincture with it, whereby the great treasure reveals itself unspeakably, with great power.

## The 5th Process.
### An Augmentation for Gold.

Take 1 lb. of strong <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum Vini*; ethanol or high-proof alcohol</note> and 8 ounces of white calcined <term>tartar</term> <note>original: *gebranten Weinstein*; potassium carbonate derived from wine barrel deposits</note>, put this into a crucible and pour the Spirit of Wine over it. Take the remaining tartar and <term>calcine</term> <note>burn to a white ash</note> it very well in a new earthenware vessel, pour warm water on it so the salt dissolves, let that run through a woolen bag, and boil that water down again; thus you obtain a subtle salt.

Also take the remaining yellow water that was separated last from the element of Water—for it belongs there and is indeed Air—fit it with a helm, and rectify the Air quite gently over. When the redness begins to rise at the very end, stop; leave the redness alone and collect it in its own glass. Repeat such rectification six more times. Every time the redness appears at the end—which is the element of Fire—collect it, until the Air has been rectified six times in this manner. Thus, you have also separated the Air from the Fire and Water, for the Air is always the **intermediary** between the Water and the Fire.

Now take the redness that you collected last from the Air during the rectification and kept in its own glass, and pour it into the element of Fire which has not yet been rectified. Then take this water, placed in a flask with a sealed helm, and set it on ashes with a small material fire to <term>digeriren</term> <note>to "digest"; to soak or heat substance gently at a constant temperature, similar to incubation</note> for a day and a night. Afterward, draw everything over quite gently until nothing remains in the flask. Pour the water back in and draw it over again until nothing remains in the flask; repeat such rectification six times, and thus everything rises over...

[Keen] knowledge: When the **helm** <note>original: *Helm*; the cap or "head" of the distillation apparatus</note> begins to "sweat," and after this sweating, drops run down inside the helm or veins [streaks] appear on the inner part of the glass, know that these are pure **Phlegmata** <note>original: *Phlegmata*; watery, inactive impurities that lack the "spirit" of the substance</note>. But when you no longer see the running veins and drops trickling down, and the helm becomes clear, then the Phlegmata have been separated from the **element of Water**. You should then immediately—yet quite gently and slowly—distill this over completely into a prepared and well-sealed **recipient** <note>original: *Recipient*; the glass vessel that catches the condensed liquid</note>, so that the **spirits** <note>the volatile, active essences</note> do not escape.

If, during this distilling and drawing over, you see that the element of Water (which is white) finally transforms into yellow drops, and that the helm has also colored slightly yellow, then remove the recipient containing the element of Water and plug it well. This is the first labor of its **rectification** <note>original: *Rectification*; the process of refining a substance through repeated distillation</note>. To further rectify or cleanse this water, you must **reiterate** <note>distill the same liquid again</note> it upon itself seven times; then the element of Water is rightly and thoroughly purged. But mark this: when you have removed the recipient with the element of Water and the yellow drops begin to come, place another recipient (as previously mentioned) to receive the yellow water. Understand clearly that you must catch the remaining yellow water in its own glass, for it belongs to the **element of Air**. As I have reported before: the element of **Water** is white, the element of **Air** is yellow, and the element of **Fire** is red. The fourth element is the **Earth**, and it is black. Thus, in the division, separation, and rectification of the elements, you must pay close attention to the color if your work is to proceed successfully.

Therefore, catch the remaining yellow water in its own glass and guard it well. When you must repeat this rectification with the element of Water, note that you should always collect and catch the remaining yellow water together in one glass; for through this work, the yellow water (which is the Air) is separated cleanly from the element of Water. If you do this as I truthfully instruct you here, you are working correctly. And just as you have performed and repeated this labor with the element of Water in its rectification six times, always separating the element of Air from it, you must proceed in the same manner with the other two elements, Air and Fire. If any of the element of Fire—which is the redness that appears on the helm and in the drops—should come into the element of Air (that is, if any such redness enters the yellow water, namely the Air), then separate these two elements exactly as you first [separated] Air and Water...

## Address of the Goddess Pallas to the European and Asian Goldmakers, as they appeared before her throne.

Earthly-minded mortals! What drives you to turn from your great Creator toward His creations? What deceptive hopes lead you to abandon your proper calling and seek refuge in chemistry and alchemy? <note>original: "Chy- und Alchymie"</note> What have you achieved until now with all your laboring <term>Laboriren: the physical work of alchemical experimentation, often involving dangerous or expensive furnace work</term> other than exhausting yourselves, and what continues to blind you? Since you know that all your previous works have ended fruitlessly, why do you now fall anew into even more errors? As we can see from all the so-called chemical processes you have brought with you: How long? How long will you rage with fire and flame, with glowing heat and coals, against the metals, against nature, and against me myself? Yet, this time we will look upon your simplicity with sympathetic, even merciful eyes, provided that you satisfy the command we reveal to you and render due obedience. For you do not know what you seek, and you do not understand your own work. Therefore, instead of an answer to the processes you brought—which are entirely unfounded in nature—take only as much as Apollo will now tell you concerning gold; then you shall see how far you wander from the goal you have set for yourselves.

Thereupon Apollo stepped forward and spoke of gold in the Latin language, using only these few yet emphatic words:

### On Gold <note>original: "De Auro"</note>

> Our gold is threefold, <note>original: "Aurum nostrum est triplex"</note>
> ->Solar,<-
> ->Astral &<-
> ->Metallic.<-
> **Solar** gold is the finest and purest, stripped of all dross. <note>original: "Solare; est finissimum, purissimum, omnibus scoriis exutum."</note>
> **Astral** gold is carried in its vehicle; it is mixed so that it can be communicated to the matrix. Both [Solar and Astral] are highly volatile and are the first agent. <note>original: "Astrale, fertur vehiculo suo, & est mixtum, ut matrici possit communicari, utrumque est volatilissimum, & primum agens."</note>
> **Metallic** gold: It lies hidden indeed in the bark <note>The "bark" or "cortex" refers to the outer, base material or ore that hides the true metallic essence</note>, but it does not yield to the enemy, nor to Vulcan <note>Fire</note>, nor to Mercury, over both of which it has triumphed since the creation of the world, and held in derision. <note>original: "Metallicum: Latet quidem in Cortice, sed hosti non cedit, neque Vulcano, neque Mercurio, de quibus à Creatione Mundi triumphavit, & irrisui habuit"</note>

## Mandate of the Goddess Pallas.

### To the European and Asian Chemists and Alchemists.

We, Pallas, hereby command in the name of all goddesses and gods—as we seek to promote human salvation and well-being—all and every experimenter, chemist, and alchemist, and those who have until now worked with chemical fires and the supposed gold-makers in both Europe and Asia, that they shall not only cease and desist from their deceptive fire-works; but we also will and hereby make known that in the future, no one, whoever they may be, shall be permitted to engage in chemical labors unless they have first been examined before our throne by Apollo and found fit for such important work. But whoever shall act against this our command and dare to undertake even the slightest of the aforementioned labors further shall know that he is not only to expect our wrath in the most sensitive manner, but that all the elements <note>original: "Elementa"</note> shall pursue and oppose him: The air shall become water to him, the water earth, the fire air, and the earth fire. This mandate was written out in duplicate, <note>original: "in duplo"</note> and one was then given to the European and the other to the Asian gold-makers, along with the necessary travel money and orders to deliver it to their chemical colleagues and to make the will of Pallas known with emphasis. After this promise, they took their leave <note>The German text ends with "beurlaubten," matching the catchword from the previous page's metadata.</note>

### Address of the Goddess Pallas to the European and Asian Gold-makers, as they appeared before her throne.

Earthly-minded humans! What drives you to turn from your great Creator toward mere created things? What deceptive hopes entice you to abandon your proper vocation and seek refuge in chemistry and alchemy? What have you accomplished until now with all your laboring, other than wearing one another out? And what continues to blind you? Though you know that all your previous works have proved fruitless, you now fall into new and even greater errors, as we can see from these so-called chemical processes <note>original: "Processe," referring to specific alchemical recipes or formulas</note> you have brought with you. How long? How long do you intend to rage with fire and flame, with glowing heat and coals, against the metals, against nature, and against me myself? 

Yet, for this one time, we shall look upon your ignorance <note>original German "Einfalt" can mean simplicity or foolishness</note> with eyes of compassion, even pity—provided that you fully satisfy and offer due obedience to the command we are opening to you. For you do not know what you seek, and you do not understand your own work. Therefore, instead of an answer to the processes you have brought—which are entirely groundless in nature—take only what Apollo will now tell you concerning gold; then you shall see how far you wander from the goal you have set for yourselves.

Hereupon Apollo stepped forward and spoke of gold in the Latin language, using only these few yet emphatic words:

->### Concerning Gold.<-

> Our gold is threefold:
> ->Solar,<-
> ->Astral, and<-
> ->Metallic.<-
> Solar gold is the finest and purest, stripped of all dross. <note>original Latin: "Solare; est finissimum, purissimum, omnibus scoriis exutum."</note>
> Astral gold is carried in its own vehicle and is mixed so that it can be communicated to the womb <term>matrix: the "womb" of the earth or a vessel where minerals were thought to gestate</term>; both of these are highly volatile and are the primary agents. <note>original Latin: "Astrale, fertur vehiculo suo, & est mixtum, ut matrici possit communicari, utrumque est volatillissimum, & primum agens."</note>
> Metallic gold: This truly lies hidden in the outer casing <note>original Latin: "Cortice," literally "bark" or "rind," referring to the external physical form of the metal</note>, but it does not yield to any enemy, nor to Vulcan <note>the Roman god of fire, here symbolizing the alchemist's furnace</note>, nor to Mercury <note>referring to quicksilver</note>, over which it has triumphed since the creation of the world, and held in derision... <note>original Latin: "...& irrisui habuit"</note>

# First TREATISE.

### Arnold of Villanova
<note>Arnold of Villanova (c. 1240–1311) was a famous physician, alchemist, and astrologer. This text attributes to him the "Microcosm" theory, which was a cornerstone of medieval and Renaissance science.</note>

Description of the correspondence or agreement between the great and small worlds; namely, how the human body governs itself and is a successor to the great world, and that within the small world—that is, man—there is to be found exactly what the great world contains within itself.

### In the World.

| Physiognomy, or the shape of the face. <note>The practice of assessing a person's character or fortune from their outer appearance, especially the face.</note> | The appearance of the heavens. |

For just as there is a manifestation of storm and thunder in the great world, so too is there the seizure or the falling sickness in humans. And just as the storm alters and weakens the animal senses and understanding—as can be observed in the unusual crowing of roosters, the strange cries of other birds and animals, and even in the tiny, raging gnats when a storm is brewing—so it is also with those afflicted by seizures.

### In the Great World.

1. A change in the air occurs when a storm arises.
2. Clouds gather.
3. The wind.
4. The crashing and thundering.
5. The hailing and lightning.
6. The rain.
7. The surges of the river. <note>original: "Schläge des Fluß"; refers to the violent flooding or "striking" of rising waters.</note>

The quarries, which are the bones of the Great Mother. <note>In alchemical and classical thought, the "Great Mother" is the Earth (Gaia/Terra).</note>

### In the Small World.

1. A change in reason when a seizure occurs.
2. Dark eyes; sleep.
3. Bloating of the neck and the belly.
4. The bursting of bubbles and the shaking of the body. <note>Early medical theory suggested that internal "vapors" or "bubbles" caused the tremors of a seizure.</note>
5. Fiery and shimmering eyes.
6. Foam. <note>Referring to the frothing at the mouth common during a grand mal seizure.</note>
7. Constricted spirits <note>original: "Spiritus"; the "vital spirits" or subtle energies believed to flow through the nerves to control movement.</note> that tear at the limbs within the enclosed skin.
8. Returning to reason and speech.

Namely, when the person comes to themselves again, and the sun of the small world—which is reason—restores the understanding and other functions of the body to their former state after the required rest.

The bones in the flesh. For just as the earth is secured with stones, so also is the body protected with bones, which are compared to gold, as being of the same nature. <note>In alchemical correspondence, bones are the most "fixed" and durable part of the body, just as gold is the most durable and "perfect" metal.</note>

| **The Weeping Woman.** | Of the pruned grapevines. <note>original: *Wein-Reben*. This is a play on words: a pruned vine "bleeds" sap, which was commonly described as the vine "weeping" (*weinen*).</note> |

| **A Praiseworthy Marriage: Mutual Love.** | Of the ring-necked doves, which are the most chaste among birds. |

Regarding this species of dove, Aelian <note>original: *Elianus*; referring to Claudius Aelianus, a Roman author and teacher of rhetoric whose work *On the Nature of Animals* was a standard source for animal lore.</note> writes—and it is also well known—that they remain together out of a special love as if they were actually married. They live in such <term>chastity</term> <note>In this context, it refers to monogamous fidelity.</note> that neither goes to another for a mate. However, if they are led astray by untimely love, the others sitting nearby will tear them apart. The doves cannot bear for their mates to pair with others or to abandon the marriage established from the beginning, unless they are unpartnered or widowed. They are entirely pure from adultery: for the male never leaves the partnership once begun, except through death; and the female also never separates from him, unless she becomes widowed. During the laying of eggs, the male is present, attending to and caring for his mate in the best possible way. If the female does not wish to go to the nest, the male strikes her with his wings and compels her into it. When she has laid the eggs, he forces her, as it were, to brood, and they both brood one after the other: the male by day and the female by night. If the male dies, the female abstains from all food and drink for a long time, mourning and grieving. The love of doves for one another is so great that the female does not let the male leave her until he has first "billed" her <note>original: *geschnabelt*; referring to the "billing and cooing" behavior where birds touch beaks before mating.</note>.

Of the green meadows, which are painted with flowers of every color, representing their own inexpressible transformation.

Of the chamois <note>original: *Gämbsen*.</note> and the cranes; for the cranes cry out when they notice something. They keep watch during the night, and so that they might be more secure in this, they take a stone into their claws; if it falls from them in sleep, it accuses them of negligence <note>This is a common motif in medieval and Renaissance bestiaries: the crane's stone serves as a "living alarm clock" to ensure the sentry stays awake.</note>. They elect a leader from among themselves, who must keep watch and give the signal through his crying while the rest of the flock sleeps. When they fly, they have certain ones appointed in the rear guard to cry out to them, and with such shouting, they keep the flock together. When they descend to the earth, the leader makes a great cry so that they all come together and graze with one another. Now, when this leader becomes hoarse and weary from the terrible shouting, another takes his place. When they are on the move, they form a triangle out of a naturally clever deliberation, so that they can more easily part the air coming against them. Thereafter, they gradually lift the course of their wings from both sides with their feathers, as if with oars. When the weather is unstable and a wind rises, they do not stretch out forward (though they fly curved like the moon when it is still), but rather press straight through like a wedge. When they see that the eagle is coming too close to them, they form themselves into a ring and wheel about like a sickle into a battle formation <note>original: *Schlacht-Ordnung*.</note>, at which point the eagle retreats. While flying, they rest their necks upon the backs of those flying ahead (and the stags do this as well when they swim through a river), making the effort easier for them; and when the first one is tired, he moves to the back. Of cats.

<margin>Scuffling has shown the way to those who quarrel</margin>
The domestic roosters; for when they fight one another, they are quite warlike, arrogant, and stubborn in combat. Nature has granted them an advantage, for they alone among all winged animals wear a comb instead of a helmet, have spurs on their feet, and spread the feathers on their neck and nape apart like a mane when they wish to fight. When they walk over a threshold, even if the door is ever so high, they nonetheless stoop out of pure haughtiness, so that they might not accidentally strike their comb. When they gain the upper hand in combat, they seek to make themselves so large with flaming eyes, ruffled feathers, curved tails, and rising cries, just as if they wished to represent a triumphant conqueror. But the defeated one slinks away in silence and, as if full of melancholy, enters into servitude.

## The Adepts.
<note>In this context, "Adepts" refers to alchemists or Hermetic philosophers who have achieved a high level of secret knowledge, particularly regarding the "Philosopher's Stone" or the "Elixir of Life."</note>

The Philosophical Hermetic Adepts have learned the practice of renewing youth from the sea-bird **Halcyon**, <note>The Kingfisher, often associated with calm seas and mythical restorative powers.</note> the eagle, the crab, snakes, and similar animals: which shed their old skin almost every year, renew their age, and become young again, as it were. Since we now see that this is permitted to irrational animals, why should it not be possible for man, who was indeed created in the image of God and possesses reason?

The eagle casts off old age by shedding its feathers and becomes young again. Snakes leave their skin in the springtime, and another grows in its place; they surpass the deer in renewing themselves: and they are good for the renewal of our bodies and hold back old age. For prudent Nature shows and proves through this how many animals there are, such as snakes and vipers; <note>original: "Eyderen," likely a variant of "Eidechsen" (lizards) or "Ottern" (vipers).</note> among the sea creatures, the aforementioned **Locusta**, <term>Locusta</term> <note>In early modern natural history, this term often referred to a type of lobster or large crustacean rather than a grasshopper.</note> crabs, and chickens, <note>The mention of chickens here refers to the molting process where they shed and replace feathers.</note> who pull off their skins in spring and autumn and cast off their old shells, thereby reminding humans that the property they possess will also be useful and good for them—namely, for the peeling and renewal of the skin. The deer, when it notices that old age presses upon it and falls too heavily, swallows a snake that resists and has been killed by its feet; and when it has survived the poison, it becomes young again through its consumption.

Through the example and prudence of these irrational animals, humans have been moved and encouraged so that they too, for their own best...

### The Sigils of Raphael <note>Raphael is traditionally the Archangel of healing and the ruler of the Sun or Mercury in various Hermetic traditions; here, the associations follow specific talismanic traditions.</note>

When the image of a dragon is engraved into a ruby or another stone of a similar nature, know that its power is to increase the goods of this century <note>i.e., material wealth in this lifetime</note>, and to make and keep the one who wears it fresh and healthy.

When the image of a donkey is carved into a chrysolite <note>A yellowish-green gemstone, often peridot.</note>, it gives the one who carries it the power to proclaim future things (at least as much as human weakness is permitted to speak concerning the future <note>original: "de Futuris"</note>), for truly, proclaiming future things belongs to God alone.

When the image of an astrolabe <term>astrolabe: an ancient astronomical instrument used to solve problems relating to time and the positions of the stars and sun</term> is carved into a garnet, its power shall be to make the one who wears it healthy, and to free them from all kinds of illnesses and adverse accidents.

# Ram.

The image of a ram, or even a human head with a beard engraved into a sapphire, has the virtue of healing and freeing one from many infirmities; it also possesses very singular powers when treated in another manner, which, however, is neither useful nor permitted to reveal to everyone <note>The author frequently alludes to "secret" or "forbidden" knowledge that is withheld from the general public to maintain the mystery or safety of the practice.</note>.

# Fish.

The figure of a fish, engraved into the stone beryl, has the power to reconcile enemies and to establish friendship among people.

# Camel's and Goat's Head.

When a camel's head and those of two goats are carved into an onyx under the image of a myrtle tree, it has the power to call together, assemble, and drive spirits together if one carries it; it also causes one to see terrifying and wonderful things in sleep.

# Bat.

When the image of a bat is engraved into a heliotrope <note>original: "Sonnen-Würbel," literally "sun-vortex" or "sun-turner." This refers to the gemstone Heliotrope (also known as bloodstone), which was anciently believed to turn the sun red when placed in water.</note>, it enables the wearer to resist spirits.

# A Person's Image.

The image of a well-dressed person, holding something beautiful in their hand, engraved into a carnelian and carried on one's person, has the power to resist spirits, to staunch blood <note>In the "Doctrine of Signatures," the reddish color of carnelian was believed to give it power over blood-related ailments.</note>, and helps one to attain honor.

# Of Lions and Archers.

When the image of the lion <note>Referring to the zodiac sign Leo.</note> or the archer <note>Referring to the zodiac sign Sagittarius.</note> is engraved into a stone and carried on one's person, it helps against poison and resists fevers.

### A Person Armed with Bow and Arrow.

The image of a person armed with a bow and arrow, engraved into an Iris-stone <note>original: "Iris," likely referring to iris-quartz or an iridescent gemstone believed to contain the colors of the rainbow.</note>, has the power to preserve the one who wears it, and the place where it is kept, from unfortunate accidents and difficult times.

### The Image of a Person with a Sword in Hand.

When the image of a person with a sword in hand is engraved into a carnelian, it has the power to protect and free the place where it is from hail and storms, and it protects the wearer from vices and sorcery.

### Image of an Ox.

If the image of an ox is placed within horehound <note>original: "Andorn" (Marrubium vulgare), an herb traditionally used in folk magic for protection and to break enchantments.</note>, it helps against sorcery and brings favor from craftsmen regarding their masterworks <note>This implies the talisman helped apprentices or journeymen gain approval from their guild masters.</note>.

### Hoopoe.

When the form of a hoopoe, with the herb dragonwort <note>original: "Dracontia," likely referring to *Dracunculus vulgaris* or a similar "serpent-like" plant.</note> before it, is engraved in a beryl stone; it has the virtue of summoning water spirits, forcing them to speak, and obtaining answers from them regarding whatever they are asked.

### Image of a Person with an Uplifted Hand.

When the image of a person, with the right hand stretched upward toward heaven, is engraved in a chalcedony, its virtue is to settle civil disputes, to make the wearer healthy, and to protect them from all dangerous accidents on travels (after God <note>The author adds this parenthetical to ensure the magical power of the stone is seen as secondary to Divine will.</note>).

### Biblical Names.

When Biblical names are engraved into a thunderstone <note>original: "Ceraunia," stones—often prehistoric tools or fossils—historically believed to have fallen from the sky during lightning strikes.</note>, it has the power to protect the place where it is from thunderstorms; and it grants those who carry it power and victory against their enemies.

### Images or Sigils of Chael.

Chael, one of the sons of the children of Israel and the eldest doctor <note>original: "Doctor," used here in the sense of a learned teacher or sage.</note>, while he was in the desert, perceived and had many figures engraved according to the course of the signs <note>original: "Zeichen," referring to the signs of the Zodiac.</note> and the planets. He noticed that a very great and extraordinary power was hidden within them. In order that the virtues of these images would be revealed to posterity, he produced his own book about them, which was found after his death; the following pieces are taken from that same book: And God be praised, who has given such virtues to the world for the salvation and benefit of the human race. These words appear right at the beginning of the book which Chael compiled. The elders of the children of Israel, and those into whose hands it fell after his death, hesitated for a long time before they were willing to share <note>original: "communiciren," meaning to share or publish.</note> this manuscript, until finally, through various occurring calamities <note>original: "Fatalitæten," meaning unavoidable disasters or events of fate.</note>, it was gradually revealed.

## The Sigils and Images of Solomon.

Although many Sigils <note>original: "Sigilla" — symbolic seals used in ceremonial magic to command spirits or represent divine forces.</note> and Pentacles <note>original: "Pentacula" — talismans, often circular, inscribed with complex geometric and linguistic symbols used for protection or evocation.</note> of Solomon are known to the Magi and Cabalists <note>original: "Magis und Cabalisten" — practitioners of high magic and Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), respectively.</note>, which they use in their sciences, the following have perhaps least often come to hand. Know therefore, kind reader, that an ancient manuscript was found among the children of Israel in the wilderness, in which much was contained concerning the works of Solomon, which descendants have communicated to one another from time to time, and which is believed to have been written by Solomon’s own hand. The title of this manuscript is: **Of the Seals of the Stones according to Your Name, O Lord, and according to the Course of the Stars.**

### The Fiery Triplicity.

This consists of: The figures of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius <note>The three zodiac signs associated with the element of fire</note>, engraved into a gemstone, set in silver, and carried upon one's person. Due to the influence of the planets that hold dominion over these signs, it dispels phlegmatic diseases <note>illnesses believed to be caused by an excess of the "phlegm" humor, often characterized by coldness and sluggishness</note>, provided it is engraved correctly.

### The Image of the Earthly Triplicity.

This consists of: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn <note>The three zodiac signs associated with the element of earth</note>, engraved into a gemstone and carried upon one's person. It resists "hot" diseases <note>feverish or inflammatory conditions</note> and makes everyone who carries it skillful in plowing, sowing, and planting—particularly in cultivating and establishing vineyards. However, much depends on the quality of the engraving.

### The Airy Triplicity.

This consists of: The images of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius <note>The three zodiac signs associated with the element of air</note>, engraved into a gemstone, set in brass, and carried upon one's person. It removes cold and dry humors <note>referring to the melancholic bodily fluid in traditional medicine</note> and is beneficial to sailors who intend to sail with all winds. All who carry it are freed from the danger of water, but it must be engraved with great care and by one who understands astronomy <note>in this context, "astronomy" includes the astrological knowledge of celestial timing</note>.

### The Watery Triplicity.

This consists of: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces <note>The three zodiac signs associated with the element of water</note>, engraved into a gemstone, set in tin, and carried upon one's person. It resists "hot and dry" diseases and all adverse ailments stemming from the bile <note>the "choleric" humor</note>. However, one must not keep this stone on their person for long, as it brings about harm alongside its benefits, causing one to become inconstant and an enemy of the truth.

### The Image of Saturn.

The image of Saturn <note>The Roman god and planet associated with time and discipline</note>, which is commonly depicted as an old man holding a scythe in his hand and having a beard that is not overly thick. This figure, engraved into a stone that is of the nature of Saturn <note>such as onyx or lead-colored stones</note>, makes the wearer powerful and increases their prosperity and advancement, provided it is engraved into a suitable stone at the proper astrological time and hour.

### The Image of Jupiter.

The image of Jupiter is formed in the likeness of a man sitting upon a throne, holding a scepter in one hand and a pillar in the other; or as the <term>Doctores Magicæ</term> <note>original: "Doctores Magicæ"; the learned teachers or masters of the magical arts</note> otherwise depict him. If one has such an image engraved into a gemstone and set in English tin <note>likely high-quality pewter, which was associated with the planet Jupiter</note> so that the stone, thus prepared, can be worn as a ring; then know that he who carries it upon himself shall acquire favor and goodwill among both spiritual and worldly persons <note>meaning both the clergy and the secular nobility or public</note>. However, this engraving must be performed at the proper time and hour <note>referring to the astrological hour when Jupiter is in a strong celestial position</note>. If one wears such an engraved stone upon the head, it also strengthens the memory in a singular and wonderful way.

### The Seal of Mars.

The image of Mars <note>original: "Sigillum Martis"</note>, which is formed in many ways, must always be engraved into a gemstone while depicted in armor. Whoever carries such a stone, in which the image of Mars is engraved, shall become courageous and overcome his enemies in battle, especially when this image is engraved at the right time into a stone of similar virtue <note>a stone naturally aligned with Mars, such as hematite or carnelian</note>.

### The Seal of the Sun.

The image of the Sun <note>original: "Sigillum Solis"</note> is likewise found in various forms, which are not unknown to the <term>Magis</term> <note>original: "Magis"; magicians or practitioners of natural magic</note>. Whoever carries this image engraved into a gemstone at the proper time and hour, especially when it is set in good, pure gold, shall be pleasing to both the great and the small; indeed, everyone will seek his favor and company. Furthermore, this image has many more uses, though for fear of its misuse, one has rightfully hesitated to fully disclose either the figure itself or its complete effects.

### The Seal of Venus.

The image of Venus <note>original: "Sigillum Veneris"</note>, engraved into a gemstone, set in copper, and carried upon one's person—its virtue and effect is: to carry out one's business well and bring it to a desired conclusion. This image also frees one from the peril of water <note>original: "Wassers-Noth"; danger of drowning or disasters at sea</note>, provided it is engraved into a stone at the proper time and hour.

Whoever carries this shape engraved into a gemstone attains thereby skill and understanding to perceive things otherwise unknown to him and to fathom hidden matters.

### The Image of the Crown.

When this image is engraved into a gemstone, it gives to the one who carries it honor, favor, and knowledge.

### Serpentarius.

Serpentarius <note>The Serpent Bearer, now commonly known by the Latin name Ophiuchus.</note> is the figure of a man who holds a serpent by the head in his right hand and by the tail in his left; he is in the sign of Scorpio and in the northern <note>original: "Mitternacht," literally "midnight," used historically to denote the North</note> part. He has the nature of Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Saturni und Martis"</note>. This image, engraved into a gemstone and carried upon oneself, has the power to heal the bites of venomous animals and snakes; if one places this stone in water or wine and drinks from it, then all ingested or drunk poison must pass away through vomiting without harm.

### The Eagle.

The Eagle, or falling vulture <note>In historical astronomy, the constellation Aquila was often called the "Flying Vulture," while Lyra was the "Falling Vulture." The arrow, however, is of the nature of Mars and Venus <note>original: "Martis und Veneris"</note>. When these aspects are carved into a gemstone, they maintain the one who carries it in his honorable status and make it so that he becomes a lord and conqueror of his enemies.

### The Dolphin or Fish.

The Dolphin or Fish is the likeness of a hump-backed fish; it stands in the sign of Aquarius and in the northern part. It has the nature of Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Saturni und Martis"</note>. This image, carved into a stone, makes the one who carries it successful in fishing and is generally good for those people who travel upon the water.

### Pegasus.

Pegasus, or the winged horse, stands in the sign of Aries and in the northern part. It has the nature of the sea <note>original: "Meeres"; this may be a scribal error for the planet Mercury (*Mercurii*), as these descriptions usually list planetary natures.</note> and Jupiter <note>original: "Jovis"</note>. When it is carved into a gemstone, it grants the one who carries it luck and victory in field battles to overcome enemies. One can also make a horse courageous with it if one hangs the aforementioned image, engraved in a stone, around its neck.

### Cetus.

The Whale <note>The constellation Cetus, often depicted as a sea monster.</note> is the figure of a large fish with a curved tail and a large mouth. It is located in the sign of Taurus and in the northern <note>original: "Mitternächtigen Theil," literally the "midnight part," which historically refers to the North.</note> part, and has the nature of Saturn <note>original: "Saturni"</note>. This image, when engraved into a stone, makes the one who carries it fortunate during travels upon the water and the sea.

### Orion.

The figure of Orion is the image of an armed man with a sword or a sickle in his hand; it is placed in the sign of Gemini and in the northern part. It has the nature of Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars <note>original: "Jovis, Saturni und Martis"</note>. This figure, engraved into a gemstone, has the power to overcome one’s enemies for the person who carries it.

### Likeness of the Ship.

The likeness of the Ship <note>The constellation Argo Navis, which was later divided into several smaller constellations.</note> is a ship with a curved prow and with oars. It is contained within the sign of Leo and in the northern part; it has the nature of Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Saturni und Martis"</note>. This, when engraved into a gemstone, makes the one who carries it safe and fortunate upon the water and the sea.

### Shape of the Dog.

The Dog <note>Likely Canis Major or Canis Minor.</note> has the shape of a harrier or greyhound with a curved tail; it stands in the sign of Cancer, in the southern <note>original: "Mittägigen Theil," literally the "midday part," referring to the South.</note> part, and has the nature of Venus. This figure, engraved into a gemstone, frees the one who carries it from various accidental illnesses.

### The Shape of the Hare.

The shape of the Hare <note>The constellation Lepus.</note> is in the likeness of a hare with pricked-up, pointed ears and feet positioned as if it were in full flight. It is placed in the sign of Gemini and in the southern part; its nature is Saturnine and Mercurial <note>original: "Saturninisch- und Mercurialisch"</note>. It has the power, when this figure is engraved into a gemstone and worn by someone, to free the one who carries it from many kinds of illnesses and from evil spirits.

## Proof of why Magical Images possess such great power and effect.

The cause for why—and from where—the rings, images, and figures engraved into a certain stone or metal derive the great powers and effects mentioned above is not to be attributed to their temperaments, nor their obvious qualities, nor their complete physical essence. Rather, it is to be attributed to a Divine and Magical—that is, a higher—cause from above. Some have not unreasonably called this the <term>Vehicle</term> <note>original: "Fuhrwerck," a term used in Hermetic philosophy to describe the medium or "chariot" through which celestial influence travels to the material world.</note> and the <term>Bond</term>. By means of this, body and soul—two essences standing apart from one another—are linked together. With this, the magnet draws iron; and the chicory <note>original: "Wegwarten." Folklore often claimed this flower could follow the sun or unlock hidden powers.</note> aligns itself with the course of the sun.

These secrets, though they have lain hidden and concealed until these recent times, have been misused by some rather than used lawfully. # The Fourth Treatise

## Description of some select medicines, which the highly experienced naturalists <note>original: "Naturkündiger"; those who study the secrets of the natural world, often through an alchemical lens.</note> of former times used.

### Preceding necessary, useful, and sincere instruction on the preparation and composition of chemical medicines.

Although every physician <note>original: "Medicus"</note> experienced in chemistry <note>original: "Chy- und Alchymia"</note> and alchemy is sufficiently capable of making his own medicines—or having them made—without the following guidance <term>manuduction</term> <note>From the Latin 'manuductio', literally 'leading by the hand'; a step-by-step guide or manual.</note>; and is even in a position to give me further instruction in chemistry, alchemy, and the preparation of chemical medicines; nevertheless, I am well aware that for those once-renowned, learned, and experienced physicians, time is far too precious and noble. Indeed, it is almost impossible for them to set pen to such matters and write various chemical reports, as they have enough to do with their medical practice <note>original: "Praxi"</note> and are otherwise overwhelmed with business <note>original: "Affaires"</note>. In truth, they can create more benefit for themselves and the public <note>original: "Publico"</note> if they serve the sick daily with tireless, faithful counsel, rather than having to withdraw from the world, as it were, through extensive writing.

However, these men will not object if I hereby spare them this labor, as a service without profit. Just as I ask no special thanks for it and will be gladly satisfied if I only do it correctly; if anyone finds the following unappealing, I ask them for better instruction and such correction that I may say: "Let the righteous and learned man rebuke or remind me kindly." <note>A humble reference to Psalm 141:5, often used by early modern authors to invite constructive criticism from peers.</note> Although this is not my own work, but only a small labor compiled by me from various manuscripts <note>original: "Manuscriptis"</note> of learned people and naturalists; nevertheless, I hope to serve the beginner in chemistry and alchemy and earn some thanks, because through this shared information <note>original: "Communicatum"</note>, I will at least open his eyes so far that he may—much sooner than without guidance—proceed to the preparation and composition—

[the] composition of chemical medicines <note>original: "Chymischen Artzeneyen"</note>, can achieve but a little; especially as it is not in everyone's power to acquire the otherwise expensive chemical books—of which there has certainly been no lack until now, nor will there be in the future. And even if I deserve no thanks for this, it is nonetheless my duty to serve my ignorant neighbor—who perhaps longs for such things but cannot attain them due to the hatred and envy of others.

Therefore, kind reader, know that chemistry <note>original: "Chy-"</note> and alchemy, insofar as they serve the art of medicine, teach the way and manner of preparing medicines in the best possible way; that is: to separate and divide the pure from the impure; to transform foreign properties or even to take them away entirely; to make the fixed volatile and the volatile fixed <term>fixation and volatilization</term> <note>These are core alchemical processes: 'fixing' means making a substance resistant to heat, while 'volatizing' means making it easier to evaporate or transform into vapor.</note> (as medicines often lack both), and finally to make everything more agreeable and pleasant to nature. This is done so that the medicines may work all the better and with less danger within the human bodies—which is the proper work of medicine—and may transform them or make them healthy. Because this art is so excellent and possesses such special power after its preparation, artists have kept it secret or have so hidden and obscured their revelations and writings that access to the preparation of said chemical medicines has been almost entirely denied to those inexperienced in chemistry and alchemy. Thus, no one could attain this science except those experienced in the origin and knowledge of nature. For this reason, I have been moved all the more to grant my ignorant neighbor some instruction, namely that which follows and has already been mentioned.

## Chemical and Alchemical Instruction.

The matter and material <note>original: "Materia und der Zeug"</note> with which chemistry and alchemy must deal in order to produce good medicines is threefold:
1. The Animal Kingdom <note>original: "Regnum Animale"</note>, the kingdom of animals or the animals themselves.
2. The Vegetable Kingdom <note>original: "Regnum Vegetabile"</note>. The soil or the plants of the earth.
3. The Mineral Kingdom <note>original: "Regnum Minerale" </note>. The mineral realm, or the minerals.

## The Earth-Growths are:

Those that draw their nourishment from the earth through seeds or planted roots: And these are trees, shrubs, and all herbs, which are called **growing things** by Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine.</note>; because they wither from year to year and grow forth again.

## The Minerals are.

Those found in the entrails of the earth, formed from the mixing of earth and water according to the various interactions of those things, and found congealed into different forms and types.

->Of these, there are three lineages.<-

The Metals.
The Middle-Minerals, and
The Stones.

### Metal.

A metal is a body that is mined <note>original: "gegraben," literally "dug."</note>, by nature liquid or hard, which can nevertheless be melted or made soft; such as gold, silver, tin, lead, copper, and iron.

## The Middle-Minerals.

The middle-minerals are all **marcasites** <term>marcasites</term> <note>In early modern chemistry, this term was used broadly for pyrites and various ores that had a metallic luster but were brittle.</note>: such as those of gold, silver, lead, and tin. Also antimony <note>original: "Spießglaß"</note>, magnesia, tutty <term>tutia</term> <note>A zinc oxide byproduct of smelting, often used in healing salves.</note>, orpiment <term>operment</term> <note>A deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral.</note>, arsenic, alum, sulfur, and the like. They are called "middle" because they possess an intermediate nature between metals and stones: they melt like metals, but they cannot be worked with a hammer; instead, they shatter like stones.

Stones are certainly distinct from metals; as they

## Consideration of those things and means which a Chemist <term>Chymicus</term> must use to prepare and produce a medicine from the aforementioned materials.

### The actual Chemical Instrument.

The actual chemical instrument (as well as the instrument of nature) is fire—not, to be sure, taken in the strict sense as we usually use it only for a visible thing, but for all heat that proves the power of a fire and produces such works and things.

->A dry one, and<-

->Immediate.<-

And it is of
->Three grades or stages.<-
The first is that which is enough to set the work in motion; the second is that which can carry on and finish the same work with a small addition.
